purpose: Single source of truth for the CPU and memory the release admission gives each container it starts while it builds a release on the production host (root ADR-0134 §3, ADR-0137). scripts/deploy/foundation-release-admission.py reads it from the control checkout; tools/host-memory-budget.contract.json counts it as a one-shot job.

publisher.memory_reason: Measured on ai-server on 2026-10-03 for release 451ee512, same image, CPU quota and job count: anonymous memory peaked at 17,914,359,808 bytes (16.7GiB), 19.9GiB with page cache, and the build took 2,590 s. Most of it is the bundled DuckDB C++ build (libduckdb-sys). 22g is the anonymous peak x1.3. The 4g that ADR-0134 set thrashed for an hour without finishing.

tippecanoe.memory_reason: Measured on ai-server on 2026-10-03 with infra/tiles/tippecanoe/Dockerfile, the same buildkit image, 2 CPUs and MAKE_JOBS=2: anonymous memory peaked at 838,496,256 bytes (1.87GB with page cache) and the build took 114 s. 1200m is the anonymous peak x1.3 (root ADR-0138). make -j"$(nproc)" saw every host core inside the CPU-quota builder, so the job count is fixed here.

dependency_resolver.memory_reason: spark-submit only resolves the engine's Ivy packages into an empty cache; no Spark work runs. Unchanged from ADR-0134.

build_cache.reason: The publisher's dependency cache lives under /var/lib/perfectory on the host's root disk (the only root-owned path the admission accepts), and that disk ran out twice (2026-10-02). A new cache is exported only when, after it reaches max_bytes beside the kept one, at least min_free_bytes (20 GiB) stay free; an exported cache larger than max_bytes (15 GiB) is discarded instead of kept. Either way the release still builds; it only rebuilds the dependency layer next time (ADR-0155).

artifacts_from_means: Where release admission takes a release's executable, jars and images (root ADR-0276 §4, §10). server-build: it builds them, as before. registry: it pulls the release CI built and signed from GitHub's container registry by digest and verifies it offline before it installs anything (stage R3, once verify-registry has passed on ten releases, stage R2). Switching back is the rollback.

registry.reason: Root ADR-0276 §3, §5: the package under the canonical repository's owner (tools/github/repository-identity.json) holds every release as <commit>-<image> and release-<commit>; the signature must name this workflow on this ref and the commit being installed. scripts/ci/release-push.sh writes the package this names; the trusted root is Sigstore's public-good instance, pinned, changed only by a pull request.
